title.narrative: Community-Led Lifesaving Response for Communities in Rural Jowhar District Affected by Multiple Shocks and Conflict.

description.narrative: ltpgtThe project aims to restore livelihoods, improve food security, and reduce flood-related risks for vulnerable rural households in flood-affected riverine communities of Jowhar District. Recurrent seasonal flooding has resulted in widespread crop losses, damage to productive assets, reduced income opportunities, and increased food insecurity, placing households at heightened risk of displacement and negative coping strategies. These impacts disproportionately affect female-headed households, minority groups, and households with persons with disabilities, who face structural barriers to accessing resources, land preparation services, and income-generating opportunities.ltbrgtThe intervention is informed by findings from the completed Flagship Community Engagement (CE) process and Area-Based Coordination mechanisms, which identified livelihood recovery and flood risk reduction as priority needs in CE-validated high-risk locations. Based on these findings, the project delivers an integrated package of time-bound, community-led Food Security and Livelihoods interventions that address both immediate recovery needs and prevention of further losses.ltbrgtKey activities include provision of agricultural inputs and land preparation services to enable timely restoration of crop production short-term income support through Cash for Work linked to community-prioritized activities and implementation of light flood mitigation works to protect agricultural land, productive assets, and access routes from recurrent flooding. Cash for Work is applied both as an income stabilization mechanism and as a means to support community-led rehabilitation of flood protection structures, ensuring dual benefits at household and community levels.ltbrgtProtection mainstreaming, Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP), and Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) measures are integrated across all components. These include protection-sensitive targeting and delivery arrangements, accessible complaints and feedback mechanisms, and clear communication with communities regarding entitlements, implementation schedules, and reporting channels. This approach ensures that assistance is delivered safely, equitably, and with dignity, while strengthening trust and accountability.ltbrgtThe project will be implemented over a six-month period, commencing following grant approval and rolling disbursement under the SA2 Envelope 2 allocation. Phased implementation is aligned with seasonal priorities, allowing early livelihood recovery actions to precede the main Cash for Work and flood mitigation phase, followed by monitoring, validation, and learning. Implementation through Area-Based Coordination structures will ensure coherence with other Flagship-supported interventions, avoid duplication, and promote coordinated response at local level.ltbrgtBy combining livelihood recovery with flood risk reduction and protection-sensitive delivery, the project contributes to reducing food insecurity, safeguarding productive assets, preventing further livelihood losses, and strengthening the resilience of vulnerable communities in flood-prone areas of Jowhar District, in line with the objectives of the SHF SA2 Flagship.ltbrgtltbgtThe project will be implemented in the CE-validated riverine villages of Bulo Feermo, Micituure, Kulmis Weyn, Ali-Warabay, and Timire in Jowhar District.lt/bgtltbrgtlt/pgt
